newsitem.title: USA: US growth near trend in Q2 1997 -- Fed's Meyer.
newsitem.headline: US growth near trend in Q2 1997 -- Fed's Meyer.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer said on Wednesday that U.S.economic growth had slowed to close to its trend rate in the second quarter and was likely to continue along that path throughout this and next year.

"The economy appears to have slowed to near a trend rate in the second quarter," Meyer said in prepared testimony to the House Banking Committee. "I do not see any obstacles to the continuation of the expansion, with growth near trend, through 1998."
Meyer said the recent experience of high growth coupled with low inflation did not suggest that the concept of NAIRU, or non-accelarating inflation rate of unemployment, was dead.
"I continue to believe NAIRU is an important and useful concept, and...I believe NAIRU has declined from about 6 percent at the end of the 1980's to about 5.5 percent currently," he said.
At NAIRU, unemployment is believed to be at a point consistent with a constant rate of inflation.

Meyer said recent economic performance in the United States had been "puzzling" and was due to both temporary supply shocks as well as "longer lasting", structural factors such as higher productivity.

However, Meyer warned that the Fed would not sit by and let the economy expand unchecked to the point where inflationary pressures emerge. "Monetary policy should not sit on interest rates and wait until the economy blows by capacity and inflation takes off," he said.
